note: Concept to simulation map. PhET slugs are taken verbatim from PhET's own browse pages; every slug is re-verified over HTTP at runtime because an invented or retired slug would present a dead iframe as a lesson resource. Gizmos entries are titles only: Gizmos is proprietary and per-seat, so a launch is a deep link into the subscriber's own signed-in session and never an embed.

phet.telemetry_api: None in the free CC BY-NC sims. Real-time data streams / API control / event logging require PhET-iO, which is a SEPARATELY LICENSED (paid) product.
phet.attribution: Simulation by PhET Interactive Simulations, University of Colorado Boulder, licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0. https://phet.colorado.edu

gizmos.public_url_pattern: https://www.explorelearning.com/index.cfm?method=cResource.dspDetail&ResourceID=<id>  (ResourceID resolved at runtime; list is publicly browsable without login)
gizmos.license: Proprietary. Subscription / per-seat license (Terms & Conditions of Use, last updated August 2026).
gizmos.documented_api: LTI 1.3 / LTI Advantage (Deep Linking optional), OneRoster via LTI or SAML, Clever Roster, ClassLink API, SAML SSO. These are institutional integrations, not a public content API.
gizmos.attribution: Gizmos is a proprietary product of ExploreLearning. Access is authorised by the operator's own subscription.

mappings.why: Models an equation as a balance scale so students manipulate both sides to isolate the unknown.

mappings.sim_title: Exploring Linear Inequalities in One Variable
mappings.sim_slug_or_id: Exploring Linear Inequalities in One Variable
mappings.why: Directly targets graphing and solving one-variable linear inequalities with a guided lab.

mappings.concept: Solving & graphing systems of linear equations
mappings.why: Explore slope/intercept interactively, the visual foundation for graphing systems.
Purpose-built for two-variable linear systems; also has Standard Form and Matrices variants.
Machine metaphor maps an input to exactly one output, the core definition of a function.
Domain/range and function-vs-relation reasoning with graphs, tables and rules.
Extends simplification to integer and fractional exponents; companion 'Exponents and Power Rules'.
Area model makes polynomial multiplication and factoring visually concrete.
Algebra-tile modeling of factoring; companion activity for ax^2+bx+c.

mappings.concept: Graphing quadratic functions / vertex & standard form
mappings.why: Directly manipulates a,b,c to show how each coefficient reshapes the parabola.
Connects factoring, the quadratic formula and x-intercepts of the graph.
Builds both sequence types and contrasts recursive vs explicit forms.
Play with slope and intercept to connect equations to lines.

mappings.concept: Center and variability / mean, median, spread
mappings.why: Visual, manipulable dot plots make mean/median/MAD intuition concrete.

mappings.concept: Scatter plots, correlation & lines of best fit
mappings.why: Drag points and fit a line to see how outliers move the regression line.
Galton board builds binomial distributions empirically from random trials.
Coordinate-geometry practice deriving distance between two points.

Sliding a book/pushing a crate exposes static vs kinetic friction and coefficients.

Listen and see how frequency/amplitude map to pitch and loudness.

Trace a laser through media of different indices; measures angles directly.
Principle-ray diagrams for lenses/mirrors with object-image geometry.

Change masses and separation to see F proportional to m1*m2/r^2.

3D builder shows how bonding/lone pairs set geometry and bond angles.
Shows electronegativity difference, dipole moment and resulting polarity.

Sandwich/real-reaction analogy visualizes limiting reagent and leftovers.
Mass <-> moles <-> particle-count conversions; companion Stoichiometry Gizmo.
Manipulates P, V, T to fit gas-law relationships; companion Ideal Gas Law Gizmo.
Add solute/solvent/water to see how concentration changes; Molarity is the quantitative version.
Test everyday substances' pH and dilution effects on the log scale.

Disturb an equilibrium and watch it re-establish; companion Equilibrium and Pressure.
Microscope view of plant/animal/bacterial cells with organelle close-ups.
Particle-level view of passive/active transport and concentration gradients.

Builds the cyclical relationship and balances the photosynthesis/respiration formulae.
Construct a DNA molecule and model replication; pairs with RNA and Protein Synthesis.
Molecules flow through transcription and translation to make a protein.
Breed mice and observe dominant/recessive ratios; companion Two Traits Gizmo.

Assemble a food web and trace energy/death effects; companion Pond Forest/Prairie Ecosystem.

Block-coding a Mars rover: sequencing, loops and debugging in a concrete task (grades 4-6).

Tracks phase changes and energy in the hydrologic cycle; companion Water Pollution, Freezing Point of Salt Water.

mappings.concept: First law of thermodynamics / internal energy of an ideal gas
mappings.why: Gas Properties models an ideal gas with controllable volume, temperature and particle count, so internal energy and heat/work exchanges are observable. It approximates the first law rather than isolating it; slug verified live (HTTP 200) on 2026-10-11.

Greenhouse Effect lets learners compare atmospheric compositions and observe surface temperature response. It covers the greenhouse mechanism, not the full carbon cycle; slug verified live (HTTP 200) on 2026-10-11.
